pairs.question: Pater, licet aliquid interrogare?
pairs.derivation: The monk Ouini, prostrate before the dying bishop Ceadda, asks permission to put a question. Framing 'et prosternens se in terram :' and the interior 'Obsecro,' inquit,' is dropped, leaving the speaker's own interrogative 'pater; licet aliquid interrogare?' (first word capitalized). Ceadda's reply 'Interroga,' inquit, 'quod uis.' has its tag 'inquit' dropped, leaving 'Interroga, quod uis.' Stops there, before Ouini's next request 'At ille: Obsecro, ut dicas...'

pairs.question: Obsecro ut dicas, quod erat canticum illud laetantium, quod audiui, uenientium de caelis super oratorium hoc, et post tempus redeuntium ad caelos?
pairs.answer: Re uera autem angelorum fuere spiritus, qui me ad caelestia, quae semper amabam, ac desiderabam, praemia uocare uenerunt, et post dies VII se redituros, ac me secum adducturos esse promiserunt.
pairs.derivation: Ouini asks what the heavenly song was that he had heard come over the oratory. The interior tag 'inquit' is dropped; 'Obsecro ut dicas' is the speaker's own plea forming the question and is kept. Ceadda's reply is introduced by the tag 'Respondet ille:' (dropped). His first sentence 'Si uocem carminis audisti, et caelestes superuenire coetus cognouisti, praecipio tibi in nomine Domini, ne hoc cuiquam ante meum obitum dicas.' is a non-answering preamble (a command not to tell), so the answer start is advanced to the operative answering sentence 'Re uera autem angelorum fuere spiritus...' which directly identifies the song as angelic spirits. That sentence runs to the end of the reply; it is the whole answer.

pairs.question: Quid debeo cantare?
pairs.derivation: In the Caedmon episode, after the visitant insists Caedmon must sing, Caedmon asks what he should sing. The interior tag 'inquit' is dropped, leaving the interrogative 'Quid debeo cantare?'. The reply 'Et ille, Canta, inquit, principium creaturarum.' has its framing 'Et ille,' and 'inquit,' dropped, leaving 'Canta principium creaturarum.' The earlier exchange ('canta mihi aliquid' / 'Nescio cantare...' and 'mihi cantare habes') is a command-and-refusal, not an interrogative, so it is not extracted. Stops at the end of the answer, before the narration 'Quo accepto responso, statim ipse coepit cantare...'

pairs.question: Et quare non citius hoc conpertum mihi reuelare uoluisti?
pairs.answer: Timui propter reuerentiam tuam, ne forte nimium conturbareris.
pairs.derivation: Abbess Aebbe of Coldingham asks Adamnan why he did not reveal his vision to her sooner. The framing 'Dixit autem abbatissa:' is dropped, leaving the direct interrogative. His reply 'Qui respondit:' (dropped) opens with the operative answer 'Timui propter reuerentiam tuam, ne forte nimium conturbareris.' (to the first full stop). The continuation 'et tamen hanc consolationem habeas, quod in diebus tuis haec plaga non superueniet.' turns from answering the 'why' to offering consolation, so the window ends at the first full stop.
